title: Valentine's Day
tagline: Flowers on the table. Dinner on the way.
about: One busy Valentine's Day in Los Angeles follows a florist and a big tangle of couples falling in and out of love.
cue: Serve dessert when Julia crashes Harrison's dinner as a waitress.
faces: “Love is the only shocking act left on the planet.”

    StartersReed's flower shop goat's cheese toastsSourdough hearts with whipped goat's cheese and chilli honeyHow to make it8 slices of sourdough2 tbsp olive oil150g goat's cheese, soft50g cream cheese3 tbsp honey1/2 tsp chilli flakes1 small bunch thyme1 punnet edible flowersCut hearts from the sourdough, brush with oil and toast at 190°C until crisp.Whip the goat's cheese with the cream cheese until smooth.Warm the honey with the chilli flakes.Spread the toasts with the cheese, drizzle with hot honey and scatter with thyme leaves and edible flowers.Reed's flower shop zucchini flowersZucchini flowers filled with ricotta and lemon, fried in a light batterHow to make it12 zucchini flowers250g ricotta40g parmesan, grated1 lemon1 basil100g plain flour170ml cold soda water500ml vegetable oil, for fryingMix the ricotta, parmesan, lemon zest, chopped basil and pepper.Remove the stamens and spoon a little filling into each flower, twisting the petals closed.Whisk the flour and cold soda water into a thin batter.Heat the oil to 180°C. Dip the flowers in batter and fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp. Drain.Salt lightly and serve with lemon wedges.MainsValentine's sirloin with garlic butterSirloin steaks with garlic butter and crisp smashed potatoesHow to make it800g baby potatoes3 tbsp olive oil4 sirloin steaks70g butter2 garlic cloves, crushed1 small bunch thyme150ml red wine150ml beef stock300g green beansBoil the potatoes until just tender, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with oil and roast at 220°C.Season the steaks and sear in a hot pan on both sides.Add most of the butter, the garlic and thyme and baste briefly. Rest the steaks.Add the wine and stock to the pan and reduce by half.Saute the beans in the remaining butter. Serve with the steaks and potatoes.Edgar and Estelle's anniversary salmonEdgar and Estelle, back together after a rough Valentine's DayHow to make it4 salmon fillets, skin on1 tbsp olive oil800g kipfler potatoes2 bunches of asparagus1 shallot80ml white wine vinegar100g cold butter, diced1 lemon1 chivesBoil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender, then halve them.Simmer the chopped shallot in the vinegar until almost gone, then whisk in the butter a piece at a time over low heat with a squeeze of lemon.Salt the salmon skin and cook skin side down in the oil for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip for 2 minutes.Blanch the asparagus for 2 minutes.Plate the salmon on the potatoes and asparagus, spoon over the sauce and scatter with chives.SweetsValentine's red velvet cupcakesRed velvet cupcakes with cream cheese frostingHow to make it175g butter, soft (115g for the cakes, 60g for the icing)200g caster sugar2 eggs1 tsp vanilla extract1 tube red food colouring paste200g plain flour2 tbsp cocoa powder1 tsp bicarbonate of soda160ml buttermilk1 tsp white vinegar200g cream cheese250g icing sugarBeat the cake butter with the sugar, add the eggs, vanilla and red colouring.Fold in the flour, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda and the buttermilk mixed with the vinegar.Divide into cupcake cases and bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Beat the cream cheese, remaining butter and icing sugar until fluffy and pipe on.Crumble one cupcake over the rest to finish.Pistachio chocolate-dipped strawberriesStrawberries dipped in dark chocolate and chopped pistachiosHow to make it500g strawberries, stalks on150g dark chocolate50g pistachios, finely chopped50g white chocolate10g freeze-dried raspberries, crushedWash the strawberries and dry them completely.Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl over simmering water.Dip each berry two-thirds of the way in, let the excess drip off and roll the base in pistachios. Lay on baking paper.Melt the white chocolate and drizzle over with a fork, then dust with crushed raspberry.Chill until set.DrinksKara's I Hate Valentine's Day pink fizzSparkling rosé with grapefruit juice, raspberries and rosemaryHow to make it12 raspberries120ml pink grapefruit juice480ml chilled sparkling rose4 small sprigs of rosemary500ml pink lemonade (for anyone not drinking)Drop raspberries into each flute and add a splash of grapefruit juice.Slowly top with chilled sparkling rose. For anyone not drinking, use pink lemonade instead.Rub a small rosemary sprig between your hands and add one to each glass.
